title: A musician's day, pay and chaperoned dances
summary: He earned $3.33 a date, played eight to one every day, and dances were attended by women with chaperones under high moral standards.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I see. Macho, tell me about a musician's day at that time. When did it start, when did it end, how much were you paid?
Well, when I was working for the Sexteto Nacional I have about $3.33, three dollars and thirty-three cents.......
Okay. How .......
.....for, for dates.
Okay. How - when did you start playing? What time in the evening?
What time? From eight to one.
Eight to one. And all the dance floors closed at one or did another band take over?
No, practically everyone was closed at 1:00 o'clock....
.... because that was from Monday to Monday, everyday.
I see, I see. Everyday then.
Uh - huh
Okay. Ah - there were women chaperoned?
Yeah, many, many women that was accompanied by their mother or their aunts because there wasn't, the economy wasn't too good so they allowed the daughter or the niece to go and make some money.
Oh, you mean dancing?
Dancing.
Yeah, but what about - were there any other single girls going there like to meet men? or you know.
No.
No. Okay. Was that because the strict...
Yeah.
.....religious beliefs?
The, the moral standard was high.
